nodes.label: Persistent andaru-lab VM 114
nodes.community_name: Root-selected release with bounded automatic fallback
nodes.rationale: Owner-requested persistent development lab rather than a disposable one. Snapshot rollback itself was not exercised.

nodes.label: retainPreviousRuntime and requiresInternet as recovery requirements
nodes.community_name: Root-selected release with bounded automatic fallback
nodes.norm_label: retainpreviousruntime and requiresinternet as recovery requirements
nodes.rationale: These flags express requirements, not evidence of implementation. Verified binaries and images are retained by immutable identity, and repair must work without Internet access.

nodes.label: Container images retained by resolved identity or digest
nodes.community_name: Root-selected release with bounded automatic fallback
nodes.norm_label: container images retained by resolved identity or digest
nodes.rationale: An image tag alone is insufficient for recovery.

nodes.label: Explicit lifecycle and recovery ownership
nodes.community_name: Root-selected release with bounded automatic fallback
nodes.rationale: Applications own migrations and host package management owns install trust. Offline recovery retains a compatible executable and data pair, not merely the latest package.

nodes.label: Root-selected release with bounded automatic fallback
nodes.community_name: Root-selected release with bounded automatic fallback
nodes.norm_label: root-selected release with bounded automatic fallback
nodes.rationale: Release selection happens before the new start loads credentials, avoiding a new-binary with old-credential ordering mistake. The root recovery helper is platform code, not an extension callback.

nodes.label: Restart limit is not a general watchdog
nodes.community_name: Root-selected release with bounded automatic fallback
nodes.norm_label: restart limit is not a general watchdog
nodes.rationale: Restart accounting covers only a bounded window; later failures spaced beyond that window are not caught.

nodes.label: Offline image recovery from retained archives
nodes.community_name: Root-selected release with bounded automatic fallback
nodes.norm_label: offline image recovery from retained archives
nodes.rationale: Recovery metadata must keep the registry reference, expected image ID, archive checksum and a controlled local alias. A registry digest is not automatically a loadable local archive name.

nodes.label: Failed apply restores prior runtime without claiming success
nodes.community_name: Root-selected release with bounded automatic fallback
nodes.norm_label: failed apply restores prior runtime without claiming success
nodes.rationale: A successful fallback is recovery from a failed apply, never a successful apply of the requested settings. Recovery must re-authorize secret and certificate access.

nodes.label: Container runtime supervised with Compose provider
nodes.community_name: Native runtime as dedicated restricted systemd service
nodes.norm_label: container runtime supervised with compose provider
nodes.rationale: Compose is a container workload provider, not a peer runtime type. Environment changes take effect through recreation.

nodes.label: Native runtime as dedicated restricted systemd service
nodes.community_name: Native runtime as dedicated restricted systemd service
nodes.norm_label: native runtime as dedicated restricted systemd service
nodes.rationale: Andaru exposes start, stop, restart and status. The executable may be a packaged launcher under the same restricted identity, not a privileged hook.

nodes.label: Native add-ons as an equal execution path
nodes.community_name: Native runtime as dedicated restricted systemd service
nodes.norm_label: native add-ons as an equal execution path
nodes.rationale: Native add-ons are not a fallback for failed containers. They run as separate restricted services under the same schema-driven UI and API authorization.

nodes.label: Native Traefik as reference add-on beside Compose
nodes.community_name: Native runtime as dedicated restricted systemd service
nodes.norm_label: native traefik as reference add-on beside compose
nodes.rationale: Shared settings, permissions, secrets, logs, metrics and recovery ownership, with different artifact and lifecycle execution.

nodes.label: Reject duplicate environment or argument bindings
nodes.community_name: Native runtime as dedicated restricted systemd service
nodes.norm_label: reject duplicate environment or argument bindings
nodes.rationale: Two properties bound to the same environment variable or CLI option in one launch are rejected. Property order never decides which value wins.

nodes.label: Builder owns application configuration generation
nodes.community_name: Native runtime as dedicated restricted systemd service
nodes.rationale: Andaru adds no preparation-script API, application-migration runner, configuration-template engine or file-generation registry.

nodes.label: Native and container variants share identity and settings
nodes.community_name: Native runtime as dedicated restricted systemd service
nodes.norm_label: native and container variants share identity and settings
nodes.rationale: Only one variant runs per instance. Switching variants needs storage and compatibility preflight, not an assumption of interchangeable execution.

nodes.label: Unraid template-driven container forms
nodes.community_name: Ordered property objects with derived JSON Schema
nodes.rationale: A template binds name, default, type, mask and value to generated controls. Mask only switches password display and is not separate secret storage.

nodes.label: Ordered property objects with derived JSON Schema
nodes.community_name: Ordered property objects with derived JSON Schema
nodes.norm_label: ordered property objects with derived json schema
nodes.rationale: Authors declare types and constraints directly. Grouping and visibility guide presentation, never authorization, and the API validates every save.

nodes.label: Defaults resolved and persisted at save
nodes.community_name: Ordered property objects with derived JSON Schema
nodes.norm_label: defaults resolved and persisted at save
nodes.rationale: Explicit false, 0 and empty string are retained when valid; explicit null is rejected. Persisted settings do not change when a later manifest changes a default.

nodes.label: Enum selections as unique option arrays
nodes.community_name: Ordered property objects with derived JSON Schema
nodes.norm_label: enum selections as unique option arrays
nodes.rationale: Duplicate option values invalidate the manifest and duplicate submitted selections invalidate settings. The exact multi-selection serialization is left unspecified.

nodes.label: Presence-only argument flag binding
nodes.community_name: Ordered property objects with derived JSON Schema
nodes.rationale: Only style flag omits a false value. Ordinary boolean value arguments must not be silently treated as presence-only flags.

nodes.label: Declared property types with derived JSON Schema
nodes.community_name: Ordered property objects with derived JSON Schema
nodes.norm_label: declared property types with derived json schema
nodes.rationale: UI overrides cannot change the data type or disable validation. Conditional visibility is presentation only, never authorization.

nodes.label: Process serialization defaults for env and arguments
nodes.community_name: Ordered property objects with derived JSON Schema
nodes.norm_label: process serialization defaults for env and arguments
nodes.rationale: Locale-independent numerics, ISO 8601 dates and a sole enum value passed unchanged. Multiple enum values need explicit joining or repeated arguments.

nodes.label: Unit environment change needs service restart
nodes.norm_label: unit environment change needs service restart
nodes.rationale: daemon-reload alone left the old hostname active. A service restart activated the new one.

nodes.label: Environment change requires container recreation
nodes.rationale: Editing .env then running compose restart kept the old hostname. Recreation activated the new hostname and stopped routing the old one.

nodes.label: Environment-bound routing changes need replacement or recreation
nodes.norm_label: environment-bound routing changes need replacement or recreation
nodes.rationale: A file-provider reload does not update the environment of a running process.

nodes.label: Classify the binding rather than the Traefik feature
nodes.norm_label: classify the binding rather than the traefik feature
nodes.rationale: Environment-bound routing needs process replacement even though the file provider reloads. Install and static settings still need a restart.

nodes.label: Environment-bound routing settings
nodes.rationale: Replacing a dynamic file does not change a running process environment. The reloadable alternative renders validated routing values into the watched file; this alternative was not proven by the probe.

nodes.label: Dynamic Go templates using env function
nodes.norm_label: dynamic go templates using env function
nodes.rationale: Host rule and upstream URL were resolved from environment variables. Confirmed by a run rather than assumed from older documentation.

nodes.label: Rootful named bridge
nodes.rationale: Preserves source addresses but changed host state: created an inet netavark table and turned IPv4 forwarding on. Not to be adopted merely to recover client IPs.

nodes.label: OPNsense model-driven modules and configd
nodes.rationale: Rejects arbitrary raw service configuration because undefined input can become privileged commands.

nodes.label: FORWARD-path enforcement after DNAT
nodes.rationale: An INPUT-only drop does not block a rootful published port because DNAT moves the traffic into FORWARD. The drop must match original-direction proto-dst or it also drops response packets.

nodes.label: Container UID must match credential file owner
nodes.norm_label: container uid must match credential file owner
nodes.rationale: Container UID 0 with dropped capabilities lacked DAC override for host UID 1000 files. Running as 1000:1000 fixed it without loosening private-key permissions.

nodes.label: Extensions request approved nft resources, not global rulesets
nodes.norm_label: extensions request approved nft resources, not global rulesets
nodes.rationale: Centralized nft ownership means extensions request approved resources instead of installing their own global rulesets.

nodes.label: Page-level optimistic locking and page-scoped apply
nodes.community_name: Page-level optimistic locking and page-scoped apply
nodes.norm_label: page-level optimistic locking and page-scoped apply
nodes.rationale: A platform rule, not an extension opt-out. Apply rechecks authorized resources, constructs bindings, then restarts the process or recreates the container.

nodes.label: Active service is not proof configuration applied
nodes.community_name: Page-level optimistic locking and page-scoped apply
nodes.norm_label: active service is not proof configuration applied
nodes.rationale: Ping and active state stayed healthy through configuration problems. Andaru must validate its own declared settings and verify the intended state.

nodes.label: Declared health check required for readiness
nodes.community_name: Page-level optimistic locking and page-scoped apply
nodes.norm_label: declared health check required for readiness
nodes.rationale: Process startup and a healthy /ping do not prove every setting was consumed. The builder supplies meaningful checks; Andaru invents none.

nodes.label: Review and apply with server-derived diff and connectivity confirmation
nodes.community_name: Page-level optimistic locking and page-scoped apply
nodes.norm_label: review and apply with server-derived diff and connectivity confirmation
nodes.rationale: A browser countdown is display only. The backend decides rollback; lost connectivity means recovery status is unknown until the API is reachable.

nodes.label: Save creates pending settings; apply activates
nodes.community_name: Page-level optimistic locking and page-scoped apply
nodes.norm_label: save creates pending settings; apply activates
nodes.rationale: Pending saves, live configuration and observed state stay distinct. Saves use object versions and there is no shared candidate or draft.

nodes.label: systemd credential delivery, plain and encrypted
nodes.community_name: systemd credential delivery, plain and encrypted
nodes.norm_label: systemd credential delivery, plain and encrypted
nodes.rationale: Per-unit read-only credential files from root-only sources. Host-bound encrypted blobs are delivery artifacts, not portable backups. A key on the same disk is not whole-disk protection, and the scheme does not isolate processes sharing one UID.

nodes.label: Compose file secrets as read-only file mounts
nodes.community_name: systemd credential delivery, plain and encrypted
nodes.norm_label: compose file secrets as read-only file mounts
nodes.rationale: These are not native Podman secret storage, systemd credential delivery, per-extension ownership, rotation or revocation. The podman secret list was empty.

nodes.label: Certificate reference with separate certificate and key delivery
nodes.community_name: systemd credential delivery, plain and encrypted
nodes.norm_label: certificate reference with separate certificate and key delivery
nodes.rationale: The GUI sees references and public metadata only. Reference authorization is rechecked on save and apply, including before the private key is delivered.

nodes.label: htpasswd file binding for authorized credential material
nodes.community_name: systemd credential delivery, plain and encrypted
nodes.norm_label: htpasswd file binding for authorized credential material
nodes.rationale: Delivers existing authorized material only. It is never an instruction to store a password or hash in ordinary settings.

nodes.label: File-based basicAuth credentials
nodes.community_name: systemd credential delivery, plain and encrypted
nodes.rationale: No credentials returned 401 and supplied test credentials returned 200. Credential records must never be returned through the settings API or configuration export.

nodes.label: React + MUI Core alternative
nodes.rationale: A viable alternative: the free Table can host Andaru move and edit controls. Data Grid row drag-and-drop is a Pro feature.

nodes.label: PrimeReact and PrimeVue licence change
nodes.rationale: Current PrimeReact 11 and PrimeVue 5 publish a non-MIT licence. Not a working default for the AGPLv3 free-software goal.

nodes.label: React + TypeScript + Vite + Mantine stack
nodes.rationale: Recommended working default: a coherent MIT kit without owning every copied widget. A grid dependency is not needed for an ordered rule list.

nodes.label: React + shadcn/ui copied-source alternative
nodes.rationale: Best when source-level design control justifies owning copied components and table integration.

nodes.label: Vue + Naive UI alternative
nodes.rationale: A credible MIT alternative if its authoring style is preferred. Its DataTable does not establish keyboard-accessible row ordering.

nodes.label: Cockpit JSON page manifests
nodes.community_name: Generated management page from declarative metadata
nodes.rationale: Declares menu labels, ordering, relative pages and minimum version. Its documentation says undocumented APIs are internal and may change.

nodes.label: Generated management page from declarative metadata
nodes.community_name: Generated management page from declarative metadata
nodes.norm_label: generated management page from declarative metadata
nodes.rationale: One root menu attaches to an Andaru page. Generated settings, lifecycle and health controls sit beside a separately permission-protected application WebUI link.

nodes.label: Per-page permission mappings fail closed
nodes.community_name: Generated management page from declarative metadata
nodes.rationale: There is no implicit inheritance or public-access default. Missing access mappings and undeclared permission references are rejected.

nodes.label: Single root menu with nested page children
nodes.community_name: Generated management page from declarative metadata
nodes.norm_label: single root menu with nested page children
nodes.rationale: The root menu attaches to an existing top-level page and its children are the page definitions. This avoids a separate navigation tree or flat page registry.

nodes.label: Compose as a workload provider, not an interchangeable engine
nodes.community_name: Docker Compose 2.26.1 provider on rootless Podman
nodes.norm_label: compose as a workload provider, not an interchangeable engine
nodes.rationale: Each engine needs a proven networking model without bypassing Andaru policy. Keep Podman preferred and Docker a potential supported backend.

nodes.label: Docker Compose 2.26.1 provider on rootless Podman
nodes.community_name: Docker Compose 2.26.1 provider on rootless Podman
nodes.norm_label: docker compose 2.26.1 provider on rootless podman
nodes.rationale: Explicitly selected provider. Recommended as the next runner candidate for ordinary applications with a tested feature subset, not as Docker equivalence.

nodes.label: Script-file health check
nodes.community_name: Docker Compose 2.26.1 provider on rootless Podman
nodes.rationale: Avoids the inline-healthcheck argument problem found earlier on these runtime versions.

nodes.label: Exec-form health check argument translation
nodes.community_name: Docker Compose 2.26.1 provider on rootless Podman
nodes.rationale: Inline Python source was split into separate CMD arguments by Docker Compose, and became broken CMD-SHELL quoting under podman-compose 1.3.0. A mounted script worked. This is a tested restriction, not a repaired bug.

nodes.label: Small declarative extension manifest
nodes.rationale: Identity, required public API, menu, config schema, runtime requirements and backup ownership. A manifest requests privileges but cannot grant them.

nodes.label: Declarative add-on manifest
nodes.rationale: One descriptor drives the management page, bindings, logs, metrics, health and recovery metadata. It is a provisional example, not a finalized schema or shipped package.

nodes.label: Strict version-aware manifest validation
nodes.rationale: Unknown fields are rejected with field paths. Unsupported manifest versions are rejected, not mapped to the nearest supported version. Compatibility metadata is checked before field validation.

nodes.label: Structured settings beyond a .env interface
nodes.rationale: A small .env is not a complete reverse-proxy model. Andaru passes environment, arguments and authorized resource paths, and the builder generates application files.

nodes.label: graphify union merge driver
nodes.rationale: The driver only keeps conflict markers out of the graph; the hooks rebuild it.

nodes.label: pre-commit hook
nodes.rationale: The rebuild reads the working tree, so the hook refuses to run while there are unstaged changes or untracked files.

nodes.label: Graph corpus scope
nodes.rationale: The repository is mostly shell today, which Graphify extracts coarsely and CodeGraph does not index at all; both earn their keep as the control plane and documentation grow.

nodes.label: Tracked graphify-out/graph.json
nodes.rationale: So a fresh clone can query the graph without a rebuild.

nodes.label: Documentation nodes not refreshed by graphify update
nodes.norm_label: documentation nodes not refreshed by graphify update
nodes.rationale: The freshness gate therefore proves the code layer only; a concept removed from a document stays in the graph.

nodes.label: Leiden clustering backend
nodes.rationale: Without the leiden extra, Graphify falls back to Louvain clustering, which can produce internally disconnected communities.

nodes.label: No CI gate yet
nodes.rationale: The hooks are the only enforcement; add the same check-graph-fresh.sh run to CI once CI exists.

nodes.label: Tracked hooks replace Graphify own hooks
nodes.norm_label: tracked hooks replace graphify own hooks
nodes.rationale: graphify hook install writes post-commit and post-checkout rebuild hooks that run in the background, skip linked worktrees, and pin each machine's interpreter path.

nodes.label: Task-owned linked worktree and graph hooks
nodes.norm_label: task-owned linked worktree and graph hooks
nodes.rationale: Implementation must not build on a stale branch or another session's checkout.

nodes.label: lab-new / lab-boot / lab-console / lab-stop / lab-reset / lab-destroy / lab-list
nodes.norm_label: lab-new / lab-boot / lab-console / lab-stop / lab-reset / lab-destroy / lab-list

nodes.label: lab-run
nodes.rationale: LAB_DEADLINE is enforced inside the driver, so the session can never wait forever.

nodes.label: ANDARU_LAB_DIR layout
nodes.rationale: fw/ vendors the firmware itself, so the lab does not silently change behaviour when Homebrew updates QEMU.

nodes.label: Two-VM QEMU lab (macOS arm64)
nodes.rationale: Repeated, reproducible testing of the firewall platform against the two baselines it must handle.

nodes.label: Cloud golden preparation
nodes.rationale: Deliberately seeds no SSH keys and masks ssh.service, so SSH can never start even though openssh-server stays installed.

nodes.label: -daemonize with -serial unix server trap
nodes.rationale: The daemonized QEMU never accepts on the listening socket and reports no error, so no console output is ever delivered.

nodes.label: VM data lives outside the repository
nodes.norm_label: vm data lives outside the repository
nodes.rationale: Images, goldens, overlays, firmware variables and logs are large, host-specific and disposable, so nothing in the lab writes into the working tree.

nodes.label: apt and dpkg need </dev/null in .cmds scripts
nodes.norm_label: apt and dpkg need </dev/null in .cmds scripts
nodes.rationale: dpkg drains the queued sentinel line from the tty, so the driver aborts with lost rc sentinel; </dev/null gives an immediate EOF.

nodes.label: systemd-firstboot wizard
nodes.rationale: Left alone it leaves root with no usable password, so a later root login fails with Login incorrect.

nodes.label: Fixed NIC MAC addresses
nodes.rationale: The MACs are fixed, so interface-identity tests are reproducible: enp0s1 is always NIC 0 and enp0s2 is always NIC 1.

nodes.label: Immutable golden image
nodes.rationale: Every test runs on a copy-on-write qcow2 overlay with its own UEFI variables, because the guest writes to those too.

nodes.label: 4 KiB canonical-mode line cap
nodes.rationale: Anything longer than the cap is silently swallowed and the command never completes.

nodes.label: nc -U console transport
nodes.rationale: socat is not part of a stock macOS install, so the lab standardises on nc -U.

nodes.label: Nocloud golden preparation
nodes.rationale: The image ships no partition editor and no cloud-init, so qemu-img resize alone leaves root at 2.8 G; growpart and resize2fs are needed.

nodes.label: Lab paths not yet re-verified after move
nodes.norm_label: lab paths not yet re-verified after move
nodes.rationale: These paths were not re-executed when the lab moved into this repository and should be re-run before the lab is relied on.

nodes.label: One command per line rule
nodes.rationale: The driver appends an echo after each line, so a heredoc or multi-line construct desynchronises it; use a script pushed with emit_push.

nodes.label: Nocloud golden package residue
nodes.rationale: Purging is strictly the closer of the two to stock; leaving cloud-guest-utils installed would keep the version drift and add four extra packages.

nodes.label: Lab root password (andaru)
nodes.rationale: Trivial by design; nothing is reachable from outside the lab.

nodes.label: LAB_CMD_TIMEOUT enforced on sentinel wait
nodes.rationale: The prompt match returns immediately from a stale prompt in the buffer, so the sentinel wait is the one that spans the command runtime.

nodes.label: Serial console only (no SSH)
nodes.rationale: When the network stack is the system under test, an SSH session is part of the system under test and therefore not a trustworthy control channel.

nodes.label: User-mode netdevs without hostfwd
nodes.rationale: The guest can reach outward, but the host cannot reach in.

nodes.label: OpenWrt LuCI and ubus ACLs
nodes.rationale: ACL grants are global to the web UI and do not isolate a single page.

nodes.label: Backend-enforced extension permissions
nodes.rationale: Authenticate the extension process as well as the administrator. Opening a page must not grant arbitrary administrative power.

nodes.label: pfSense package integration
nodes.community_name: Extension code stays out of root engine and frontend
nodes.rationale: Package callbacks run inside privileged core processing. A masked password field is still stored in clear text in the XML configuration.

nodes.label: Extension code stays out of root engine and frontend
nodes.community_name: Extension code stays out of root engine and frontend
nodes.norm_label: extension code stays out of root engine and frontend
nodes.rationale: Avoid importing extension code into the root engine, exposing arbitrary execution endpoints, and raw privileged service configuration as an escape hatch.

nodes.label: No third-party JavaScript in administrator session
nodes.community_name: No third-party JavaScript in administrator session
nodes.norm_label: no third-party javascript in administrator session
nodes.rationale: Generate controls from validated metadata and link the application's own WebUI separately. An out-of-process backend does not isolate same-origin browser code.

nodes.label: No third-party JavaScript injection into admin session
nodes.community_name: No third-party JavaScript in administrator session
nodes.norm_label: no third-party javascript injection into admin session
nodes.rationale: Add-on metadata does not authorize injected JavaScript. The extension contract keeps this boundary.

nodes.label: systemd-sysext and service confinement
nodes.community_name: Signing, unit, image and hidden menus are not security boundaries
nodes.rationale: sysext merges files into host /usr and /opt, implies no security isolation, and is not a generic package or dependency framework.

nodes.label: Signing, unit, image and hidden menus are not security boundaries
nodes.community_name: Signing, unit, image and hidden menus are not security boundaries
nodes.norm_label: signing, unit, image and hidden menus are not security boundaries
nodes.rationale: Each protects a different part of the system. Systemd sandboxing must be applied to running extension services.

nodes.label: Stable extension identity independent of package name
nodes.community_name: Stable extension identity independent of package name
nodes.norm_label: stable extension identity independent of package name
nodes.rationale: Bindings and backups must not depend on a distro package name, absolute host path or internal database layout.

nodes.label: Stable property name as stored-setting identifier
nodes.community_name: Stable extension identity independent of package name
nodes.norm_label: stable property name as stored-setting identifier
nodes.rationale: The name identifies the stored setting independently of page placement and translated titles, so a moved property keeps its identity.

nodes.label: Andaru-owned systemd supervision and credential delivery
nodes.community_name: Andaru-owned systemd supervision and credential delivery
nodes.norm_label: andaru-owned systemd supervision and credential delivery
nodes.rationale: Extensions contribute scoped requests, not unrestricted unit overrides or a second packet-filter writer.

nodes.label: Dedicated non-root systemd service identity
nodes.community_name: Andaru-owned systemd supervision and credential delivery
nodes.rationale: Non-root UID, zero effective capabilities, NoNewPrivs, active seccomp and read-only system protection, confirmed by live /proc checks. Focused checks, not a sandbox escape audit.

nodes.label: Dynamic file reload keeps last-good routing
nodes.community_name: Dynamic file reload keeps last-good routing
nodes.norm_label: dynamic file reload keeps last-good routing
nodes.rationale: A malformed dynamic YAML left the previous good routing active. The invalid file on disk is still unsafe for a future restart.

nodes.label: Watched-directory dynamic reload
nodes.community_name: Dynamic file reload keeps last-good routing
nodes.rationale: The file-provider guide recommends watching the parent directory because replacing an individually bind-mounted file can break reload notifications. Bind mounts were not tested.

nodes.label: Hostname and URI format constraints
nodes.rationale: Andaru validates declared URI and hostname constraints. The builder escapes values safely in application configuration. A URL pattern alone neither validates a URL fully nor authorizes network access.

nodes.label: Schema format annotation not enforced by probe validator
nodes.norm_label: schema format annotation not enforced by probe validator
nodes.rationale: A local validator accepted an invalid value for format hostname. Production format support must be qualified before values reach routing templates.

nodes.label: Literal English or exact i18n key text
nodes.community_name: Literal English or exact i18n key text
nodes.norm_label: literal english or exact i18n key text
nodes.rationale: Only a literal string or the exact i18n object is accepted. English is the fallback locale. Translation packaging is deferred.

nodes.label: Sanitized Markdown field descriptions
nodes.community_name: Literal English or exact i18n key text
nodes.rationale: Raw HTML is disabled, unsafe link schemes are rejected, and descriptions are tied to controls with aria-describedby rather than a hover-only tooltip.

nodes.label: Private telemetry metrics endpoint
nodes.rationale: Metrics come from the internal telemetry endpoint, separate from the managed application listener.

nodes.label: Loopback Prometheus metrics endpoint
nodes.rationale: A separate loopback endpoint returned service-request metrics after traffic. It is not on the public application listener.

nodes.community_name: Task 1: bounded Debian-tool adapter for host links

nodes.label: LinkStatus snapshot
nodes.community_name: Task 1: bounded Debian-tool adapter for host links
nodes.rationale: These are observations, not immutable configuration IDs or permanent-MAC identity.

nodes.community_name: Task 1: bounded Debian-tool adapter for host links

nodes.community_name: Task 1: bounded Debian-tool adapter for host links

nodes.label: Wire contract (OpenAPI 3.1)
nodes.community_name: Task 1: bounded Debian-tool adapter for host links

nodes.label: Task 1: bounded Debian-tool adapter for host links
nodes.community_name: Task 1: bounded Debian-tool adapter for host links
nodes.norm_label: task 1: bounded debian-tool adapter for host links

nodes.label: Fixed inventory bounds
nodes.community_name: Task 1: bounded Debian-tool adapter for host links
nodes.rationale: The bounds make an unavailable inventory fail explicitly with 503; no stale snapshot cache is used.

nodes.label: Stderr diagnostic fails the inventory read
nodes.community_name: Task 1: bounded Debian-tool adapter for host links
nodes.norm_label: stderr diagnostic fails the inventory read
nodes.rationale: iproute2 can report an interrupted, inconsistent netlink dump that way even with exit status zero, so the API returns 503 rather than a potentially incomplete snapshot.

nodes.label: Fixed operational bounds (2 s, 4 MiB, 4 KiB, 5 s/8 MiB, 5 s/30 s server timeouts)
nodes.community_name: Task 1: bounded Debian-tool adapter for host links
nodes.norm_label: fixed operational bounds (2 s, 4 mib, 4 kib, 5 s/8 mib, 5 s/30 s server timeouts)
nodes.rationale: These are constants, not new settings knobs; bounds are enforced while reading, not after unbounded buffering.

nodes.rationale: Ignore unrelated ip JSON fields so distro additions do not break the read adapter; this is not the strict author-manifest parser.

nodes.label: Fixed ip read via argv, no shell
nodes.community_name: Task 1: bounded Debian-tool adapter for host links
nodes.norm_label: fixed ip read via argv, no shell
nodes.rationale: No address, route, firewall, DHCP/DNS or ownership changes; never shell, PATH lookup, direct netlink realizer or user-supplied command.

nodes.label: Review focus: cancelled request or hung child is reaped
nodes.community_name: Task 1: bounded Debian-tool adapter for host links
nodes.norm_label: review focus: cancelled request or hung child is reaped
nodes.rationale: A cancelled request or hung child command must terminate within the command deadline and reap the child.

nodes.label: Review focus: malformed ip output never becomes a snapshot
nodes.community_name: Task 1: bounded Debian-tool adapter for host links
nodes.norm_label: review focus: malformed ip output never becomes a snapshot
nodes.rationale: Malformed, oversized or internally invalid ip output must never become a partial or fabricated successful snapshot.

nodes.label: Separate application dashboard link
nodes.rationale: Andaru never forwards its login cookie or token. The link's view permission does not replace the application's own authentication.

nodes.label: Authenticated dashboard route on separate hostname
nodes.norm_label: authenticated dashboard route on separate hostname
nodes.rationale: The dashboard hostname feeds the router Host rule and the WebUI link, and the certificate must cover it. Andaru never forwards its own administrator cookie or token to the dashboard.

nodes.label: Client build embedded in Go web process
nodes.community_name: Client build embedded in Go web process
nodes.norm_label: client build embedded in go web process
nodes.rationale: Build tooling is packaging only. No Node runtime, Vite dev server, SSR server or CDN is required on the firewall.

nodes.label: Local assets under an intact script policy
nodes.community_name: Client build embedded in Go web process
nodes.norm_label: local assets under an intact script policy
nodes.rationale: Bundle fonts, icons and scripts locally. Do not relax the script policy or load CDN resources to make a demo work.

nodes.label: Ordered firewall rule table
nodes.community_name: Explicit keyboard move controls for ordered rules
nodes.rationale: Shows execution position, enabled state, action, protocol, source and destination. Counters are observed data, not part of the declaration.

nodes.label: Explicit keyboard move controls for ordered rules
nodes.community_name: Explicit keyboard move controls for ordered rules
nodes.norm_label: explicit keyboard move controls for ordered rules
nodes.rationale: Execution order is authoritative. Filtered reordering must not guess hidden positions. Native move buttons suffice; drag-and-drop is optional.

nodes.label: Compatibility via contract checks and fixtures
nodes.community_name: Compatibility via contract checks and fixtures
nodes.norm_label: compatibility via contract checks and fixtures
nodes.rationale: Promising compatibility requires contract checks and fixtures for supported manifests. Stay additive where possible; do not invent an indefinite support promise.

nodes.label: Contract frozen only at Andaru 1.0
nodes.rationale: All current examples and decisions are provisional. Pre-1.0 migration machinery is not required.

nodes.label: Typed versioned hook payloads tied to committed state
nodes.community_name: Typed versioned hook payloads tied to committed state
nodes.norm_label: typed versioned hook payloads tied to committed state
nodes.rationale: Lesson from a first-party nfSensei retrospective, not independently verified. Typed context, versioned IPC and real committed events instead of synthetic ones.

nodes.label: Independent extension updates; incompatible extension blocks core upgrade
nodes.community_name: Independent extension updates; incompatible extension blocks core upgrade
nodes.norm_label: independent extension updates; incompatible extension blocks core upgrade
nodes.rationale: Extensions update independently with administrator approval. An incompatible installed extension offers an update or explicit removal and is never silently disabled.

nodes.label: Versioned settings with application-owned migrations
nodes.rationale: Each extension has a distinct settings and secrets namespace. Andaru supplies no application-migration framework or callback runner.

nodes.label: Verified versioned Traefik release binaries
nodes.rationale: Checked against release SHA-256 lists for consistency only, not a signing identity. Both extracted ELFs were statically linked; this does not generalize to every Go build.

nodes.label: Unknown top-level static key accepted
nodes.rationale: Traefik accepted a top-level invalid key at startup. Validation inside known sections was not shown, so runtime acceptance must not be treated as validation.

nodes.label: Rootless systemd cgroups need user bus and lingering
nodes.community_name: Rootless systemd cgroups need user bus and lingering
nodes.norm_label: rootless systemd cgroups need user bus and lingering
nodes.rationale: Without a usable user bus Podman fell back to cgroupfs. A future runner must make this setup requirement explicit.

nodes.label: Default exports omit resolved secrets
nodes.rationale: Including secrets needs an explicit administrator option and a password-encrypted backup. References in ordinary settings do not export their contents.

nodes.label: Managed endpoint is a resource request, not host publication
nodes.community_name: Managed endpoint is a resource request, not host publication
nodes.norm_label: managed endpoint is a resource request, not host publication
nodes.rationale: managed does not publish a host port or grant WAN access. Port 8443 is a listener request needing conflict and firewall resolution. URL userinfo is rejected so credentials stay in secret references.

nodes.label: ACME state contains private material
nodes.rationale: If ACME is enabled, its state belongs under secret-aware backup and recovery policy, not ordinary unencrypted export.

nodes.label: API-first engine with replaceable UI
nodes.rationale: The API owns authentication, authorization, validation and state changes. The unprivileged Go web process serves UI assets while the root engine owns configuration and operations.

nodes.label: Amber accent is not body text colour
nodes.community_name: Amber accent is not body text colour
nodes.norm_label: amber accent is not body text colour
nodes.rationale: Amber on white measures 1.80:1, a static calculation rather than a rendered audit. Never convey state by colour alone.

nodes.label: Missing interfaces must not block the management path
nodes.community_name: Missing interfaces must not block the management path
nodes.norm_label: missing interfaces must not block the management path
nodes.rationale: Show an actionable degraded state with no automatic interface substitution. A failed WAN must not hide a working management page.

nodes.label: Go templates or templ with HTMX
nodes.community_name: Go templates or templ with HTMX
nodes.norm_label: go templates or templ with htmx
nodes.rationale: Legitimate but a different presentation architecture. The rule table needs fragment or small-script integration.

nodes.label: Engine and API before mockups
nodes.rationale: Core implementation is not blocked on visual approval. The presentation layer starts once secured endpoints exist.

nodes.label: Shell with brand chrome and persistent navigation
nodes.community_name: Shell with brand chrome and persistent navigation
nodes.norm_label: shell with brand chrome and persistent navigation
nodes.rationale: Dark brand chrome with a neutral content surface. Compact policy tables rather than a dashboard card per datum.

nodes.label: Server-state library only where loaders stop being clear
nodes.community_name: Server-state library only where loaders stop being clear
nodes.norm_label: server-state library only where loaders stop being clear
nodes.rationale: Choose one data approach rather than stacking Redux on top of another cache.

nodes.label: Required UI states for the first slice
nodes.community_name: Required UI states for the first slice
nodes.norm_label: required ui states for the first slice
nodes.rationale: Covers loading, conflict, saved-but-unapplied, applying, confirmed, failed, rolled-back and disconnected states.

nodes.label: Out-of-scope items for this increment
nodes.rationale: No database, configuration renderer, plugin framework, migration runner, GraphQL service, frontend build or author-CI belongs to this increment.

nodes.label: Provisional contract, no compatibility shims
nodes.rationale: Do not add compatibility shims for today's sketches.

nodes.label: Rootless named bridge network
nodes.rationale: Gives normal Compose service-name DNS, but the external client was recorded as bridge address 10.89.0.3 in ClientAddr. Unsuitable for source-IP ACLs.

nodes.label: ClientAddr peer-address verification
nodes.rationale: Traefik may overwrite ClientHost from X-Forwarded-For, so peer identity is taken from the host parsed out of ClientAddr (req.RemoteAddr).

nodes.label: Client-IP-sensitive ingress profile
nodes.rationale: Keeps ordinary isolated application networking separate from client-IP-sensitive ingress. The prior bridge still suits applications that do not depend on client IPs.

nodes.label: Guest INPUT-chain firewall rule
nodes.rationale: A dedicated INPUT drop blocked external TCP to the test ports until a source-specific allow restored access. Removing the need for a proxy header did not bypass it.

nodes.label: Rootless direct pasta network mode
nodes.rationale: Preserves the external IPv4 source address with no added host NAT or filter tables. It is an alternative to joining a named Compose network, not an option added to one.

nodes.label: Rootless slirp4netns preserving port handler
nodes.rationale: Also preserves source addresses. Its host-loopback option is an explicit extra access grant and must not become a general privilege.

nodes.label: Real socket identity over client forwarding headers
nodes.norm_label: real socket identity over client forwarding headers
nodes.rationale: Preserve real socket identity instead of accepting client-supplied forwarding headers. This removes only an IPv4/TCP blocker, not IPv6, UDP, DNS or throughput qualification.

nodes.label: Drop-then-allow firewall verification sequence
nodes.rationale: Explicit test-port drops under a default-accept chain, then source-specific accepts. Focused ingress checks, not a full default-deny policy.

nodes.label: IPv6 HTTPS ingress via direct pasta
nodes.norm_label: ipv6 https ingress via direct pasta
nodes.rationale: Preserved the external IPv6 TCP peer. Tests ingress to Traefik only, not an IPv6 upstream or multi-container service-name discovery.

nodes.label: Privileged DNS port 53 binding unqualified
nodes.rationale: Binding port 53 unprivileged is a separate privilege and socket-activation question. Only high ports were published in this spike.

nodes.label: UDP sender identity from recvfrom peer tuple
nodes.norm_label: udp sender identity from recvfrom peer tuple
nodes.rationale: The responder built replies and log records from the actual recvfrom peer tuple, never from an address supplied inside the packet.

nodes.label: UDP evidence limits
nodes.rationale: Only small single datagrams were tested. Not DNS protocol, EDNS fragmentation, QUIC, load or packet-loss evidence.

nodes.label: Guest-only nftables input drop
nodes.rationale: Dropped external connections to the published port, with a source-specific allow restoring access. Applies to this rootless topology only, not rootful bridge networking or IPv6 policy.

nodes.rationale: Exercised logs contained no supplied password, hash, private key or Authorization header. Coverage is limited to exercised requests and failure paths.
